A 22-year-old college student presents with a one-week history of fever, malaise, and severe headache
accompanied by nausea. She developed a rash four days ago and reports hiking in North Carolina two
weeks prior. She is sexually active with inconsistent barrier contraception use and lives in university
housing. Her vital signs show a temperature of 100.8°F (38.2°C), blood pressure 136/89 mmHg, pulse
84/min, and respirations 12/min. Physical examination reveals an alert patient with conjunctival
erythema, negative meningeal signs, and a bilateral blanching, macular, erythematous rash with
petechiae on wrists and ankles. Laboratory findings are: Hemoglobin: 13 g/dL Hematocrit: 39%
Leukocyte count: 9,000/mm^3 Platelet count: 85,000/mm^3 What is the most appropriate treatment for
this condition? Answer Choices: (A) Ceftriaxone (B) Penicillin G (C) Ampicillin (D) Intravenous
immunoglobulin (E) Acyclovir (F) Vancomycin plus Piperacillin-Tazobactam (G) Doxycycline (H)
Ciprofloxacin (I) Rifampin (J) Azithromycin
 A. Ampicillin
B. Intravenous immunoglobulin
C. Penicillin G
D. Acyclovir
E. Ceftriaxone
